title: cicuta maculata var. californica
intro: Cicuta maculata var. californica, commonly known as Western Water Hemlock, is a highly toxic and invasive plant species native to the western regions of North America. This plant has been used in traditional herbal medicine for its potential health benefits, which include treating fever, rheumatism, and various skin conditions. The therapeutic actions of Western Water Hemlock are attributed to its antiseptic, anti-inflammatory, and antispasmodic properties, which may help to soothe and calm the body. However, as with many toxic plants, caution must be exercised when using it, as bioactive constituents such as cicutoxin, isocicutoxin, and sesquiterpene coumarins can be highly toxic and potentially deadly in large doses.
